Our Founding Thesis

The Urban Planet
thesis.

M
Miro Cernetig CEO & Publisher — CityAge
"Cities are 3% of the Earth's surface and more than 80% of its GDP. Every structural challenge of our era — climate, capital, sovereignty — gets solved or doesn't get solved in cities."

CityAge was founded on a single observation: the decision-makers responsible for building the next century of urban infrastructure rarely get to talk to each other. Not the right ones. Not under conditions where trust gets built and deals get done.

Fourteen years and 100+ forums later, we've built the network that changes that — 25,000 verified leaders across government, capital, and industry, convened around the problems worth solving.

The Thesis

The next great infrastructure story is happening at the top of the world.

$70B+ Canada Arctic Spend
66°N Arctic Circle

The warming of the high latitudes is opening the most consequential set of infrastructure decisions in a generation. New shipping corridors. New energy grids. New sovereign claims on territory, resources, and the routes that connect the hemispheres.

For two centuries, the power centres of the Urban Planet have been in the temperate south. That is changing. The North is not a remote edge of the map — it is the next centre of gravity for capital, sovereignty, and the infrastructure that determines how nations project power and how trade connects markets.

CityAge has covered this story from the beginning. The Northern Century is our intelligence vertical and convening franchise for the people making decisions about what gets built — and what gets controlled — above the Arctic Circle.

What We Cover

Six forces shaping the North.

01 · Sovereignty

Arctic Claims & Strategic Control

Who controls the Northwest Passage, the Northern Sea Route, and the resources beneath them. The intersection of international law, military posture, and Indigenous rights in the world's last great territorial contest.

02 · Infrastructure

Ports, Corridors & Defence Build

Canada's $70B+ Arctic investment. New deep-water ports. Roads and rail into the High Arctic. The infrastructure programs that will define northern sovereignty for a century — and the capital structures that make them viable.

03 · Energy

Geothermal, Wind & Grid Independence

Iceland's volcanic grid. Scandinavian offshore wind. The energy systems that allow remote Arctic settlements and military installations to operate independently of southern supply chains — and the investment thesis behind them.

04 · Trade

Nordic-Atlantic Bilateral Networks

The Canada-Europe trade corridor. Nordic-North American industrial partnerships. How changing ice conditions are redrawing the economics of global shipping — and which ports, corridors, and nations stand to benefit most.

05 · Space

Earth Observation & the Space Economy

Arctic monitoring from orbit. The role of Earth observation in sovereignty claims, climate tracking, and resource mapping. How the space economy — satellites, launch, data — is inseparable from the future of northern infrastructure.

06 · Capital

Sovereign Wealth & Institutional Investment

The pension funds and sovereign wealth vehicles moving capital into Arctic infrastructure. How institutional investors are pricing sovereignty risk. The financial architecture funding the Northern Century — and who is positioned now.

The Arctic is not the
edge of the map.
It is the next frontier.

Arctic Circle · 66.0° N · The New Geography of Power
Why Now
"The Arctic is not the edge of the map. It is the next centre of gravity for capital, sovereignty, and the infrastructure that determines how nations project power."
— Miro Cernetig, CEO & Publisher, CityAge
Climate is opening new corridors. The Northwest Passage is navigable for longer each year. New shipping routes are being assessed — and new military infrastructure built to control them.
Canada has committed $70B+ to Arctic sovereignty. That capital is looking for industrial partners, advisors, and intelligence on where the opportunity is real.
NATO's northern flank is the new strategic frontier. Sweden and Finland's accession has changed the alliance's geography. Defence infrastructure is being built at pace.
Critical minerals are the new oil. The Arctic holds significant reserves of rare earths, lithium, and nickel powering the energy transition — and competition for them is intensifying.

The City

Where Asia meets the Americas.
And what gets built next.

Vancouver is one of the most consequential cities on Earth for a simple reason: it sits at the intersection of the world's two largest economies, on the edge of the fastest-growing ocean, in a country making enormous bets on energy, technology, and infrastructure.

No other North American city is more directly shaped by the decisions being made in Beijing, Tokyo, Seoul, and Singapore. No other city on the continent is more exposed — and more positioned — for what comes next in the Pacific Century.

The Next Vancouver brings together the leaders building that future: the investors, the ministers, the mayors, the engineers, and the founders who are deciding, right now, what Vancouver becomes.

The Format

One day.
No panels. No pitches.

The Next Vancouver is an invitation-only gathering of 100 leaders operating under Chatham House Rules. No press. No broadcasting. No keynote speakers selling their latest book.

What you get instead: a day of real conversations between people who are actually building things — and the connections that follow from that.

Invite-Only 100 Leaders Chatham House Rules One Day No Press
Who Attends

The people
building what comes next.

Ministers and senior government officials. Fund managers and institutional investors. Founders and technology leaders. Urban planners, architects, and infrastructure builders. The mayors and city-builders shaping how Vancouver grows.

Access is not purchased. It is earned through the referral chain and the verification process that has kept this network trusted for 14 years.

The First Next Vancouver

It started
here.

The inaugural Next Vancouver brought together 100 leaders for a day of conversations about the city's future — its economy, its housing crisis, its role in the Pacific, and the decisions that would define the next decade.

The conversations that happened in that room are still happening. That is what CityAge does.

Legal

Privacy Policy

Your privacy is important to us. This policy explains how CityAge collects, uses, and protects your information, in compliance with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable Canadian and United States privacy law.

This website is owned and operated by CityAge Media Inc. ("CityAge," "we," "us"). For the purposes of this policy, "the Website" refers to all websites owned by CityAge, together with our related services and products.

By using this Website, you acknowledge and accept the terms of this Privacy Policy. We may update it from time to time at our discretion; your continued use of the Website after any change constitutes acceptance of that change. We encourage you to review this page periodically.

Our Principles

  • We do not actively collect sensitive information about you, including information about your health, racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, or criminal history.
  • We take reasonable steps to protect any sensitive information we do receive.
  • We do not share your personal information with anyone except to comply with the law, deliver our services, or protect our rights.
  • We store personal information only for as long as we have a reason to keep it.
  • In our email communications, we always give you a clear way to unsubscribe.

Information We Collect

Like most website operators, we collect non-personally-identifying information that browsers and servers typically make available — such as browser type, language preference, referring site, and the date and time of each request. We use this to understand how visitors use the Website.

We may also collect potentially personally-identifying information, such as IP addresses. We do not use this to identify visitors.

When you choose to interact with us — for example, by completing a contact form — we collect personally-identifying information such as your name, email address, organisation, and message. We collect only what is necessary to respond to your request.

We do not collect or store payment or financial information. All payments — for event registration, sponsorship, or any paid product — are processed by trusted third-party platforms (such as Stripe and Ticket Tailor), each governed by its own privacy and security policies. Your card and financial details are handled entirely by those providers and never pass through or rest on CityAge's servers.

You can always decline to provide personal information, though this may prevent you from using certain features of the Website.

How We Use Your Information

We use the information you provide to respond to your enquiries, deliver and improve our services, and keep you informed about CityAge forums, intelligence, and related work — but only where you have asked to hear from us. You can opt out of these communications at any time.

Events, Photography & Chatham House Rule

When you attend a CityAge event, you may be photographed, filmed, recorded, or quoted, and that material may be used in CityAge's publications, marketing, and related communications. By attending, you consent to this use. If you wish to opt out, please let our team know in advance or on site.

Many CityAge forums operate under the Chatham House Rule, meaning information shared may be used but the identity and affiliation of speakers and participants are not to be revealed. While we ask all guests to honour this principle, CityAge cannot guarantee that every attendee will comply, and we are not responsible for disclosures made by others.

Sharing of Information

CityAge will not sell, rent, or trade your personally identifiable information to third parties.

We may share information with employees, contractors, and affiliated organisations who need it to operate the Website or deliver our services, and who have agreed to keep it confidential. Some of these parties may be located outside your home country; by using the Website, you consent to such transfers.

We disclose personal information only when required by law, or when we believe in good faith that disclosure is reasonably necessary to protect the rights, property, or safety of CityAge, third parties, or the public.

We use the following third-party service providers, each governed by its own privacy policy:

  • Vercel (hosting and privacy-friendly, cookieless analytics)
  • Supabase (data storage)
  • Stripe (payment processing)
  • Ticket Tailor (event registration and payment)

Cookies

We keep cookies to a minimum. Our analytics are privacy-friendly and cookieless, meaning we can understand general site usage without tracking you across the web or storing identifying cookies on your device. Any cookies we do use are limited to essential site function. You may set your browser to refuse or remove cookies, though some features of the Website may not function properly as a result.

Data Security

We take reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect your personal information against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. However, no method of transmission over the internet or electronic storage is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

Children's Privacy

This Website is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under the age of 16. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact us and we will take steps to delete it.

Your Rights

You may opt out of future communications, update your information, or request removal at any time by emailing info@cityage.com, or by using the unsubscribe link in our emails. Please note we may retain certain information where required for record-keeping or by law.

United States & California Residents

If you are a resident of the United States, you may have rights under state privacy laws, including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (CPRA). These may include the right to know what personal information we hold about you, the right to request its deletion, and the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information.

CityAge does not sell your personal information. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at info@cityage.com and we will respond as required by applicable law.

Your Consent

By using this Website, you consent to our collection and use of your personal information as described in this Privacy Policy.
